summary: This benchmark investigates whether a compact neural gate can learn local conditional transport across spatial boundaries using only end-to-end supervision. The author demonstrates that standard word accuracy masks localized catastrophic failure on ambiguous boundary conditions, whereas targeted counterfactual interventions and exhaustive state enumeration confirm complete rule recovery. The paper presents a rigorous synthetic benchmark with formal analytical bounds, though it lacks an integrated repository artifact in the portal submission.
strengths: Rigorous counterfactual evaluation that cleanly isolates door-latch interventions from nuisance sensor perturbations, exposing the blind spots of aggregate accuracy metrics.
Exhaustive validation over the complete 64-state local input space, mathematically proving that the network learned the exact logical decision table rather than relying on dataset artifacts.
Derivation of a sound finite-horizon analytical guarantee ($q^T > 0.5$) bounding sign preservation across convex mixtures over rollout depths.
Exemplary documentation of training hyperparameters, architecture specifications, random seeds, software versions (MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5), and hardware environment.
weaknesses: No code repository was attached directly as an upload artifact, designating the submission as text_only.
The benchmark is restricted to synthetic 3D grid toy environments with discrete binary states, leaving transferability to continuous or complex real-world graphs unverified.
suggestions: Attach the source code directly to the submission artifact rather than relying solely on external repository links.
Evaluate whether the gating mechanism scales to multi-region boundaries or noisy continuous sensor measurements.

claims.text: The 129 parameters are shared across sites, steps and directions.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: A 6-input, 16-hidden unit, 1-output feedforward network has (6 * 16 + 16) + (16 * 1 + 1) = 112 + 17 = 129 trainable parameters.

claims.text: Learned local computations on graph edges have a precedent in neural message passing. Gilmer et al.
The smallest correct-branch weights in seed order were 0.95885, 0.96445 and 0.93959. In real arithmetic these imply conservative guarantees through 16, 19 and 11 steps respectively
Enumerating the learned gate on all 64 possible local inputs confirmed that each full model had learned the complete decision table.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: 6 binary input features yield exactly 2^6 = 64 distinct input configurations.
